about.title:
Franconian roots.
European reach.
about.p1: Blüten Sturm was founded in Würzburg — a city of vineyards, baroque stone and stubborn craft. We kept the craft and added velocity. Today we work with Mittelstand leaders, challenger brands and institutions who need marketing that moves markets and teams able to carry it.
about.p2: One team, three disciplines: creative that gets remembered, strategy that gets signed off, and training that makes it stick inside the organisation.
about.f2v: German and English, plus FR · ES · IT

work.title: Recent storms.
work.p1: A family-owned Franconian manufacturer with a strong product and a name nobody outside Germany could place. Positioning workshop, new brand architecture and a bilingual identity system, rolled out across sales, trade fair and web in one season.
work.p2: A product launch in Germany, Austria and Switzerland: one creative idea, adapted per market rather than translated, with paid media, landing pages and sales material measured against pipeline, not impressions.
work.p3: Modul I and II, delivered over twelve months in German and English. New and scaling leaders in small cohorts, real cases from their own floor, and a handover so the client’s people run the next round themselves.
work.p4: Two days, three stages and a hybrid stream: concept, programme, staging and content for a client’s annual summit, produced end to end — from the first sketch to the last cable.
work.note: Case studies are anonymised here at our clients’ request. The full portfolio — names, figures and imagery — is available on request under NDA.

meta.title: The Mozart-Style Burger Stunt — the complete prompt | Blüten Sturm
meta.description: One burger, one ramp, rocket thrusters — no shoot day. How we built the Café Mozart video with Higgsfield, Nano Banana 2.1 and Kling 3.0: step by step, every prompt ready to copy.

hero.eyebrow: Free prompt · Café Mozart × Blüten Sturm
hero.title: The Mozart-Style Burger Stunt.
hero.lead: One burger, one ramp, rocket thrusters — and not a single shoot day. Here is how we built the video: step by step, with every prompt ready to copy.
hero.facts: Higgsfield · Nano Banana 2.1 · Kling 3.0 Pro · 15 sec · 9:16 · about 2 hours of work
hero.secondary: I want a video like this
hero.caption: The finished video, as it runs on @cafemozartwuerzburg.

setup.title: What you need.
setup.i1: 2–3 photos of your product. Sharp, evenly lit, shot from the angle it will have in the video. We photographed the real Mozart-Style Burger at the café — skewer, fried egg, fry basket, all of it.
setup.i2: A reference stunt clip. A clip in which one single object launches up a ramp, flies, lands and ends up standing still. Our base clip was an AI commercial with a fried-chicken bucket. No clip? Prompt 0 generates one for you.
setup.i3: A Higgsfield account. Tools used: Genjutsu “Replace Object”, Nano Banana 2.1 (image edit) and Kling 3.0 Pro (video).
setup.i4: An editor. CapCut, Premiere or DaVinci — for the cut, the title, the logo outro and the sound.
setup.note: Time: about 2 hours. Cost: a few euros in credits. Film crew: none.

steps.title: How the stunt comes together.
steps.label: Step
steps.s1p: Shoot your product against a neutral background, slightly from the side, at the product's eye level. Two photos are enough: one front-side view, one slightly higher. Rule: everything you describe in the prompt later must be visible in the photos.
steps.s2t: Pick a base clip (or generate one)
steps.s2p: The clearer the motion in the base clip, the cleaner the swap. You need one single, clearly separated object that moves as a rigid body — no hands, no people in front of it. No clip at hand? Text-to-video with Prompt 0.
steps.s3p: Higgsfield → Genjutsu → Replace Object. Upload: base clip + your two product photos. Describe your product like a food stylist would, and tell the model explicitly what must stay the same: camera, timing, ramp, light. Output: 10 seconds, 720p. Run two or three variations and keep the one where the product stays rigid and doesn't “swim”.
steps.s4p: Export the last frame of the video (screenshot or frame export). Whatever got lost in the swap — for us, the fry basket — you add back now in an image edit with Nano Banana 2.1, using the product photos as reference. 9:16, 2K, thinking set to “high”.
steps.s5p: Kling 3.0 Pro, start image = your hero still, 4 seconds, locked camera. The most important line in the prompt: the food does not move — only smoke, embers and light. That keeps the product razor sharp while the shot still feels alive.
steps.s5opt: Optional: a rocket landing as a separate shot. Start image = burger mid-air (a frame from step 3), end image = hero still.
steps.s6p: Order: launch at the ramp → flight → landing → hero shot with atmosphere → title → logo outro. Title in the brand script, logo on cream. Sound: rocket rumble, whoosh, impact — then silence for the hero shot. Export: 1080 × 1920, 24 fps, 12–15 seconds. Tip: upscale the 720p clip before the edit (Higgsfield Upscale).

template.title: Now your product.
template.text: Burger, pizza, sneaker, bottle — the template works for anything that can fly as a rigid object. Replace the placeholders in square brackets, nothing else.

tips.title: What makes the difference.
tips.i1: Describe like a food stylist. Bun, sesame, skewer, runny yolk — every detail helps the model hold on to your product.
tips.i2: “As one rigid unit.” Without that sentence, burger and fries fly separately.
tips.i3: Say what must stay. Camera, timing, light, background — not just what changes.
tips.i4: “No text, no logos.” Text comes in the edit. Never from the model.
tips.i5: Always two or three variations. The first one is rarely the best.

cta.title: Your product. Your stunt.
cta.text: We produce videos like this for restaurants, brands and the Mittelstand — in days, not weeks. Website, social media, branding: all from one team, from Würzburg.
cta.credits: Concept, prompts & production: Blüten Sturm for Café Mozart Würzburg.
